15 An airport has a mechanical system for moving luggage. The system uses a horizontal conveyor
belt, a sloping conveyor belt, a lift and a frictionless slide. A suitcase is moved around the airport
using this system.
12 m
10 m
8 m
16 m
Resistive forces opposing the motion of the suitcase are negligible.
For which movement of the suitcase is the net work done on the suitcase greatest?
A
moving the suitcase a distance of 8 m at a constant speed up the sloping conveyor belt
B
moving the suitcase a distance of 16 m at a constant speed along the horizontal conveyor
belt
C
moving the suitcase a distance of 10 m at a constant speed vertically upwards on the lift
D
moving the suitcase a distance of 12 m at increasing speed downwards on the slide

hints: Notice which movements are at constant speed and which one has increasing speed, since constant speed means kinetic energy $\frac{1}{2}mv^2$ does not change.
With resistive forces negligible, the work done on the suitcase goes into gravitational potential energy $mgh$, so compare vertical height gained, not distance along the belt.
Compare the vertical rise of the 8 m sloping belt with the 10 m vertical lift, and recall that the 16 m horizontal move has zero rise while the 12 m slide is downwards.
walkthrough: Identify the energy change: with negligible resistive forces, work done on the suitcase at constant speed equals gain in gravitational potential energy $\Delta E_p = mg\Delta h$ because $\Delta E_k = 0$.
For A, the distance along the slope is 8 m but only the vertical component counts, so $W_A = mgh_A$ where $h_A < 8\text{ m}$.
For B, motion is horizontal at constant speed, so $\Delta h = 0$ and $\Delta E_k = 0$, giving $W_B = 0$.
For C, motion is $10\text{ m}$ vertically upwards at constant speed, so $W_C = mg \times 10\text{ m}$.
For D, the frictionless slide exerts a normal force perpendicular to the 12 m displacement so it does no work, and the suitcase moves downwards so it does not gain $mgh$.
Since $10\text{ m}$ is greater than the vertical rise of the 8 m slope and greater than zero, $W_C$ is the greatest. This is option C.

A.explanation: Work done is $mgh$ where $h$ is the vertical rise, and the vertical rise for the 8 m slope is less than 10 m, so it is less than for the 10 m vertical lift.

B.explanation: There is no vertical rise and speed is constant along the 16 m horizontal belt, so change in $mgh$ and in kinetic energy are both zero.

C.explanation: Speed is constant so kinetic energy is unchanged and the 10 m vertical rise gives work $mg \times 10\text{ m}$, the largest gain in $mgh$.

D.explanation: The frictionless slide acts normal to motion so it does no work along the 12 m slide, and the suitcase loses $mgh$ while gaining kinetic energy.
